legacy_migration.trigger: A locked script establishes that one common-space information turn affects several independently acting people or clusters
legacy_migration.directing_decision: Register the table/event side, principal seating clusters, doorway, and one room master before distributing later body-state coverage; reset the master when room density or exit access changes
legacy_migration.coverage: Opening room master → table/event-side view → distinct pairs/singles by stable zone → room reset at first standing/crowding threshold
legacy_migration.blocking: Keep stable zone IDs, screen sides, chair/background anchors, and doorway access; not every person needs an isolated close-up
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Let the room become readable before the cascade; cut on a new cluster/state, not mechanically after every line
legacy_migration.sound: `UNKNOWN`; no spoken cue, silence, score, or room-tone rule is derived
legacy_migration.applicability: Public meetings, family assemblies, boardrooms, group announcements, or judged gatherings where multiple independent next-actions are locked script facts
legacy_migration.non_applicability: One person's uninterrupted performance is the primary fact; deliberate subjective confusion; or all meaningful bodies remain readable in one continuous master
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Reaction-like faces appear before geography; every person receives equal weight; actors change state synchronously; zones or doorway positions drift
legacy_migration.counterexample: `BCS-S03E05-C03-SUSTAIN-CONTESTED-PERSON-SCREEN-OWNERSHIP` is a contrary mechanism when the locked script makes one person's uninterrupted turn primary. Whether both scenes share the same dramatic trigger remains script-gated; this picture-only source cannot prove it. Same-trigger contrary evidence otherwise remains pending.
legacy_migration.unknown: Paper meaning, public status, roles, knowledge, shared stimulus, reaction causes, sound, hidden joins
legacy_migration.ai_risk: `CRITICAL`: ensemble identity, seating, eyelines, asynchronous performance, crowd density, and doorway continuity
legacy_migration.fallback: Project-original simplified floor plan with one table zone, three audience clusters, and one exit; max five identifiable people per generated shot; fixed master plus one clean view per changed cluster
legacy_migration.evidence_shots: room registration `S006–S017`; recurring clusters `S018–S064`; density/doorway resets `S065–S090`
legacy_migration.confidence: `HIGH` visible geometry/change; `MEDIUM` transfer pending locked-script trigger and contrary sources
